the observed magnetoresistance in the GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure is due to a combination of the effects of the magnetic field, the quantum size effect and the intersubband electron-electron interaction.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron mobility in a GaAs channel with a subband structure is strongly influenced by the intersubband coupling, which is not negligible in spite of a small energy difference between subbands.
the intersubband relaxation time is much shorter than the intrasubband one and that the intersubban scattering is dominant in the transport properties.

The main takeaway from our work is that
intersubband scattering is a significant source of scattering in the GaAs quantum wells with a high carrier density.
intersubband scattering can play a significant role in the transport properties of the subband structure in Si -doped FETs.
